findings.title: Cayman FATCA/CRS Compliance Form Deadline — TOMORROW 15 September 2026
findings.summary: The Cayman Islands DITC CRS Compliance Form for the 2025 reporting year is due tomorrow, 15 September 2026. This covers financial institutions' account data, due-diligence processes, and service-provider arrangements. The CRS Return itself was due 31 July 2026; this is the final remaining Cayman CRS obligation for 2025.
findings.client_impact: Any Cayman-registered financial institution, fund, or investment vehicle that is a Reporting Financial Institution must file the Compliance Form by close of business tomorrow or face penalties; FGC should confirm submission is in progress with any Cayman fund administrators today.
findings.urgency_reason: Filing deadline is tomorrow, 15 September 2026 — no extension announced.

findings.title: CIMA New AML/CFT/CPF Rule and Financial Sanctions Rule — Effective 18 September 2026 (4 Days)
findings.summary: CIMA's new AML/CFT/CPF Compliance Rule and Financial Sanctions Rule take effect on 18 September 2026 — four days from today. All CIMA-registered or licensed entities, including registered investment funds, must comply from that date. New obligations include stricter AML outsourcing standards, mandatory independent AML audits, enhanced sanctions-screening, and effectiveness testing. There is no grace period.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients with interests in Cayman-registered funds or holding vehicles must ensure their fund administrators, GPs, and directors have updated AML policies, sanctions-screening systems, and audit programmes to comply by 18 September; non-compliance from day one risks regulatory action or fines from CIMA.
findings.urgency_reason: Hard compliance deadline in four days with no grace period; fund administrators must be confirmed in-compliance today or tomorrow.

findings.title: Pillar Two GloBE Information Return — Belgium Extended Deadline 30 September 2026 (16 Days)
findings.summary: Belgium extended its GloBE Information Return (GIR) filing deadline for FY2024 to 30 September 2026 — 16 days from today. The GIR is mandatory even where transitional safe harbours apply and covers ETR calculations and top-up tax determinations per jurisdiction. The OECD Side-by-Side Package (January 2026) maps country deviations from the model rules and is a critical compliance reference.
findings.client_impact: MNE holding groups with Belgian entities (or Luxembourg entities filing into Belgium) that have not yet submitted the FY2024 GIR must do so by 30 September or face late-filing penalties; FGC clients with cross-border holding structures should confirm GIR status with their tax advisers this week.
findings.urgency_reason: 16 days to the extended Belgium deadline; late GIR filings can trigger penalties and draw FTA scrutiny of the broader Pillar Two structure.

findings.title: UAE Corporate Tax Return and Payment Deadline — 30 September 2026 (16 Days)
findings.summary: UAE entities with a 31 December 2025 financial year must file their corporate tax return and pay any liability to the Federal Tax Authority by 30 September 2026 — 16 days away. The 9% CT rate applies above AED 375,000; the 0% band applies below. The FTA is conducting active compliance audits across mainland, freezone, and offshore entities in 2026. Small Business Relief (under AED 3 million revenue) has been extended to end-2029.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients owning UAE operational entities, freezone companies, or mainland businesses must file and pay by 30 September; missing the deadline triggers late-filing penalties and heightened FTA audit risk, which the FTA is actively exercising across the UAE in 2026.
findings.urgency_reason: 16 days to filing and payment deadline; FTA audit activity makes non-compliance particularly risky this cycle.

findings.title: BCB Resolution 561 — Stablecoin/Crypto Settlement Banned from Cross-Border Payment Rails: 1 October 2026 (17 Days)
findings.summary: BCB Resolution No. 561 (30 April 2026) eliminates stablecoins and crypto assets from Brazil's regulated cross-border payment infrastructure effective 1 October 2026. From that date, fintechs and FX firms must settle the offshore leg of regulated payments using only bank wires, correspondents, or non-resident real accounts. An estimated USD 90 billion cross-border corridor is affected.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian clients or clients with Brazil-linked cash flows who currently use stablecoins or crypto payment rails for cross-border transfers must migrate to bank-wire-based settlement before 1 October to avoid regulatory non-compliance; FGC should flag this to any clients using fintech FX providers for Brazil remittances.
findings.urgency_reason: 17 days to effective date; operational changes to payment infrastructure cannot be deferred to the last minute.

findings.title: BCB Resolution 575 — New Foreign-Currency Deposit Accounts for Non-Residents Effective 1 October 2026 (17 Days)
findings.summary: BCB Resolution No. 575 (effective 1 October 2026) allows new categories of non-resident legal entities — including creditors in external credit transactions and foreign shareholders of Brazilian companies — to open and operate foreign-currency deposit accounts inside Brazil, without running through formal FX conversion for internal transfers.
findings.client_impact: Foreign clients who are shareholders in Brazilian companies or hold Brazilian credit positions can now establish BRL/FX accounts inside Brazil from 1 October, simplifying treasury management and reducing conversion costs; FGC should brief clients on account-opening procedures and integrate this into Brazil cross-border wealth structures before year-end.
findings.urgency_reason: New framework operational in 17 days; early account-opening preparations and bank engagement should begin now.

findings.title: CRS 2.0 In Effect January 2026 — Digital and Crypto Assets Now Reportable
findings.summary: CRS 2.0 is in effect from January 2026, expanding reportable assets to include digital/crypto assets and integrating with CARF. Financial institutions in participating jurisdictions must now apply CRS due-diligence to digital-asset accounts, materially widening the reporting population.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients holding cryptocurrency or digital assets through offshore accounts should expect those holdings to be reported to their home tax authority via CRS for the first time from the 2026 reporting year; FGC should advise affected clients to ensure their digital-asset positions are declared in their home-country tax filings to avoid unwanted disclosures.
findings.urgency_reason: Already in force; institutions are adapting their CRS processes during 2026, and clients have until the 2026 year-end filing cycle before first reports are submitted — but disclosure alignment should happen now, not at year-end.

findings.title: CVM Resolution 175 2026 Revisions Underway — Amendments to FIP, FIF, FII Annexes Expected Q4 2026
findings.summary: CVM's 2026 regulatory agenda signals upcoming amendments to key annexes of Resolution 175 covering private-equity funds (FIPs), fixed-income funds (FIFs), and real-estate funds (FIIs). A consultation is expected in Q4 2026. CVM Resolution 88 (crowdfunding) is also under review.
findings.client_impact: Wealth managers and family offices with allocations to Brazilian FIPs, FIIs, or FIFs should monitor the Q4 2026 consultation for structural or eligibility changes that could affect existing or planned fund investments in Brazil.
findings.urgency_reason: No immediate deadline; consultation expected Q4 2026 but not yet launched — in monitoring phase.

findings.title: Luxembourg Pillar Two Top-Up Tax Filings via MyGuichet.lu — Portal Operational Since January 2026
findings.summary: Luxembourg's Pillar Two complementary top-up tax declaration portal opened on MyGuichet.lu on 8 January 2026. Luxembourg-headquartered or locally-filing MNE groups must use this portal for GloBE compliance, following the Grand Ducal Regulation of 19 December 2025 establishing the framework. Luxembourg also introduced a new start-up tax credit and increased pension contribution rates to 25.5% from 2026.
findings.client_impact: MNE holding groups with Luxembourg entities must file Pillar Two top-up tax declarations through MyGuichet.lu; advisers should confirm that Luxembourg-domiciled holding structures are registered on the portal and that initial filings are on track for applicable deadlines.
findings.urgency_reason: Portal operational; no immediate standalone Luxembourg deadline cited — but Pillar Two filings are an active obligation and Belgium's 30 September 2026 GIR deadline may affect Luxembourg-affiliated groups.

findings.title: DIFC Variable Capital Company Regulations Enacted — 9 February 2026
findings.summary: The DIFC Authority enacted VCC Regulations on 9 February 2026, introducing a flexible multi-subfund umbrella fund structure with dynamic capital movements. The VCC competes with Singapore's structure and is designed for sophisticated portfolio management within the DIFC.
findings.client_impact: Family offices and wealth managers with DIFC-registered structures should assess whether existing DIFC vehicles could benefit from re-domiciliation into a VCC, or whether new fund launches serving UAE-based HNW clients would be better served by the VCC umbrella framework.
findings.urgency_reason: New structure enacted and available; no mandatory deadline but structuring decisions are time-sensitive for clients planning fund launches or reorganisations in the UAE.

findings.title: Malta MFSA Financial Crime Compliance Strategy 2026 and Legal Notices 82 & 83 Effective April 2026
findings.summary: The MFSA's Financial Crime Compliance Strategy 2026 and Legal Notices 82 & 83 (1 April 2026) introduce a six-pillar risk-based AML/CFT supervisory framework and amendments to AML regulations, centralised bank account registers, and internal governance. Structural reforms under Act XV 2026 created new MFSA regulatory committees.
findings.client_impact: Wealth managers and fund structures regulated by the MFSA must align compliance programmes with the new six-pillar approach, including enhanced risk-based assessments; Malta-based structures used by FGC clients should be reviewed against the updated AML framework to avoid supervisory findings.
findings.urgency_reason: In effect since April 2026; ongoing supervisory engagement against the new framework is expected to intensify through year-end.

findings.title: MAS Circular AMLD 05/2026 — Risk-Proportionate Source of Wealth Guidance; Year-End Implementation
findings.summary: MAS Circular AMLD 05/2026 (25 May 2026) guides private banks and wealth managers on applying risk-proportionate Source of Wealth (SOW) processes, discouraging blanket documentation requirements for lower-risk clients. Institutions are expected to update internal SOW procedures by year-end 2026.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients managed through Singapore-based private banks or wealth managers may experience updated onboarding and periodic-review documentation requests as institutions align SOW processes with the MAS guidance by year-end; FGC should prepare clients for potential process changes and respond promptly to any SOW requests.
findings.urgency_reason: Year-end 2026 implementation target; no immediate deadline but banks are actively updating procedures.

findings.title: Isle of Man Financial Services Bills Receive Royal Assent — Implementation Phase Underway
findings.summary: The Isle of Man Financial Services (Miscellaneous Provisions) Bill 2026, Retirement Benefits Schemes (Amendment) Bill 2026, and Verification of Entity Registration Bill 2026 received Royal Assent and are in their implementation phase, strengthening the IoM's AML/CFT framework and beneficial ownership registration requirements.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Isle of Man registered structures should confirm that their IoM resident agents have updated KYC/AML procedures and beneficial ownership filings in line with the new BO requirements under the Verification of Entity Registration Act.
findings.urgency_reason: Implementation phase in progress; compliance confirmation with IoM agents should be sought in the near term.
findings.source_name: Isle of Man Financial Services Authority

findings.title: Guernsey Registry Consultation on Expanding Beneficial Ownership Register Access
findings.summary: The Guernsey Registry is consulting on expanding BO register access beyond competent authorities to obliged entities and persons with legitimate interest. Legislative amendments are expected in 2027, following EU AMLA framework direction.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients with Guernsey holding entities, trusts, or funds should be aware that obliged entities (banks, lawyers, accountants) may gain access to their registered beneficial ownership data within the next 1–2 years; clients using Guernsey for privacy-sensitive structures should review their structures now in advance of a more accessible register.
findings.urgency_reason: No immediate deadline; consultation outcome expected to drive 2027 legislation — monitoring now allows advance planning.

findings.title: Bahamas Usufruct Interest Act 2026 and Decentralised Autonomous Organisations Act 2026 Enacted
findings.summary: The Bahamas enacted the Usufruct Interest Act 2026 (formalising usufruct estate-planning structures) and the Decentralised Autonomous Organisations Act 2026 (regulatory framework for DAO structures), part of the jurisdiction's IFC modernisation agenda.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Bahamas trusts or estate plans should ask their Bahamas counsel to assess whether the new Usufruct Interest Act offers planning opportunities (e.g., separating income rights from capital rights in structures); clients with digital-asset ventures or DAO interests now have a formal legal vehicle in the Bahamas.
findings.urgency_reason: New vehicles now available; no mandatory deadline but estate planning opportunities are time-sensitive for clients undergoing succession planning.

findings.title: Panama Enhanced BO Supervision Post-FATF Greylist Exit — Resident Agent KYC Heightened
findings.summary: Following FATF's October 2023 removal of Panama from the greylist, Panama has increased supervision of resident agents and offshore entities. The 2026 landscape requires enhanced KYC by resident agents, mandatory reporting of ownership changes, and potential local-office requirements in certain sectors.
findings.client_impact: Clients with existing Panama structures should expect their resident agents to request updated beneficial ownership documentation and KYC refreshes; FGC should facilitate a due-diligence re-assessment of any Panama holding vehicles to ensure compliance with the heightened 2026 requirements.
findings.urgency_reason: Enhanced supervision ongoing throughout 2026 following greylist exit; proactive review is preferable to a compliance gap discovered by the resident agent.

findings.title: FinCEN BOI Reporting Permanently Eliminated for US-Formed Entities and US Persons — Effective 14 August 2026
findings.summary: A FinCEN final rule (14 August 2026) permanently exempts all US-formed entities and US-person beneficial owners from Corporate Transparency Act BOI reporting. Foreign-formed entities registered to do business in the US remain reporting companies. FinCEN will delete previously reported US-person data from its database.
findings.client_impact: US-incorporated or US-domiciled clients no longer have any CTA BOI reporting obligation, removing an administrative burden; foreign-formed entities (BVI, Cayman, Panama companies) with US business registrations must continue filing and should confirm their status with counsel.
findings.urgency_reason: Already in effect since 14 August 2026; no action required for US entities — foreign-formed entities doing US business should verify ongoing compliance.

findings.title: US Estate Tax Exemption Permanently Set at $15M Per Individual Under OBBBA
findings.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 2025) permanently eliminated the 2026 sunset of elevated estate/gift-tax exemptions. For 2026 the per-individual exemption is $15 million ($30 million per couple), indexed from 2027. State-level estate taxes remain variable. Dynasty trusts and SLAT strategies remain relevant at the upper end.
findings.client_impact: US-domiciled HNW clients no longer face urgency to accelerate large gifts before a sunset date; however, clients with estates well above $15 million should continue considering dynasty trust and SLAT strategies, and those in high-estate-tax states should review state-level exposure.
findings.urgency_reason: Planning urgency from the prior sunset risk is removed; this is a stable, positive planning backdrop — no immediate action required.

findings.title: Florida SB 264 Foreign Buyer Restrictions Upheld by Eleventh Circuit — Fully Enforceable
findings.summary: The Eleventh Circuit upheld Florida SB 264 on 4 November 2025 (Shen v. Simpson), confirming the near-total ban on Chinese nationals acquiring Florida property and restrictions on nationals from Cuba, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Venezuela, and Syria owning property within 10 miles of military/critical infrastructure. Compliance affidavits are required at closing; violations risk forfeiture and criminal penalties.
findings.client_impact: Foreign national clients from the listed jurisdictions must be advised they cannot purchase Florida property (or face severe geographic restrictions), and compliance affidavits must be signed at every closing; FGC should include an SB 264 checklist in all Florida real-estate advisory work for non-US clients.
findings.urgency_reason: No new deadline — law confirmed in force; standing advisory matter for any foreign client considering Florida real-estate investment.

findings.title: FIRPTA Withholding Remains 15%; IRS Updated Forms Effective 1 January 2026
findings.summary: Standard FIRPTA withholding on US real property dispositions by foreign persons remains 15% of gross sales price for 2026. IRS issued revised procedural guidance and updated forms effective 1 January 2026, affecting withholding certificate applications and reporting procedures.
findings.client_impact: Foreign clients selling US real property must use updated 2026 IRS withholding-certificate forms; failure to use current forms can delay or invalidate certificate processing, increasing the risk that buyers withhold the full 15% rather than a reduced amount.
findings.urgency_reason: Updated forms already in effect since 1 January 2026; ensure updated forms are in use for any current or planned dispositions.

findings.title: BVI Beneficial Ownership Register Operational with Legitimate-Interest Access Since April 2026
findings.summary: The BVI's new BO registry has accepted legitimate-interest applications (banks, other obliged entities) since 1 April 2026. The register is non-public; competent authority access is standard. Entities that missed the 1 January 2026 initial filing deadline are marked 'In Penalty' and the fee/penalty moratorium ended 31 March 2026.
findings.client_impact: Clients with BVI entities should confirm with their registered agents that beneficial ownership filings are current; any entity still marked 'In Penalty' is exposed to fees, penalties, and potential strike-off, and the register is now visible to banks conducting KYC on the entity.
findings.urgency_reason: No new deadline; ongoing compliance status — but 'In Penalty' entities face ongoing risk and should be remediated promptly.

findings.title: Cyprus Major Tax Reform Effective 1 January 2026 — CIT 15%, DDD Abolished, SDC Reduced
findings.summary: Cyprus increased CIT to 15% (OECD-aligned), abolished Deemed Dividend Distribution for 2026+ profits, and reduced SDC on dividends from 17% to 5% for resident domiciled individuals, effective 1 January 2026. No inheritance, wealth, gift, or securities-CGT. Non-dom regime preserved.
findings.client_impact: Clients using Cyprus holding structures benefit from the abolition of DDD (eliminating a deemed tax on retained profits) and a lower SDC on dividends, partially offsetting the CIT increase; the overall package makes Cyprus more attractive for dividend-paying holding companies and resident non-doms, and FGC should re-model client holding structures to quantify the net impact.
findings.urgency_reason: In effect since 1 January 2026; holding-structure reviews and tax-modelling are planning work, not an imminent compliance deadline.

findings.title: Trusts (Jersey) Amendment Law 2026 — In Force 20 March 2026
findings.summary: The eighth amendment to the Trusts (Jersey) Law 1984 came into force 20 March 2026, clarifying limits on beneficiary termination rights under Article 43 and establishing priority of trustee claims vs. secured lenders under new Article 43A.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Jersey trusts benefit from greater certainty on beneficiary termination rights and trustee/lender priority, reducing litigation risk in trust administration and secured lending against trust assets; FGC should flag this to clients with Jersey structures considering secured lending or anticipating beneficiary challenges.
findings.urgency_reason: In force since March 2026; relevant for new and existing Jersey trust structures in cross-border contexts — planning matter, not time-critical.

findings.title: Swiss Voters Rejected 50% Federal Inheritance Tax — Cantonal Rates Stable; Zurich Wealth Tax Cut
findings.summary: Swiss voters rejected (78%) on 30 November 2025 a proposal for a 50% federal inheritance and gift tax on estates over CHF 50 million. Cantonal structure unchanged. Zurich reduced its wealth tax multiplier from 98% to 95% for 2026. Switzerland's Pillar Two IIR applies from 1 January 2025.
findings.client_impact: Swiss-resident and Swiss-domiciled HNW clients face no new federal inheritance tax; existing cantonal regimes (favouring spouses and direct descendants) remain intact, and Zurich-based clients benefit from a modest wealth tax reduction.
findings.urgency_reason: No action required; positive planning confirmation — removes a risk that was relevant in 2025 structuring discussions.

findings.title: MAS Asset Management Competitiveness Package — New Hedge Fund Programme and Tax Exemptions (19 August 2026)
findings.summary: MAS announced a competitiveness package on 19 August 2026 including new tax exemptions for qualifying managers, a Hedge Fund Investment Programme (MAS co-invests with managers establishing Singapore operations), and enhanced global connectivity initiatives to offset competition from Dubai and Hong Kong.
findings.client_impact: Fund managers or family offices considering Singapore as a hub for alternatives management should evaluate the new MAS co-investment programme and tax exemptions, which materially improve Singapore's economics versus Hong Kong and Dubai for hedge fund and alternatives launches.
findings.urgency_reason: Newly announced; no deadline — strategic awareness item for clients considering manager/structure domicile decisions.

findings.title: OECD Pillar Two Side-by-Side Package Released — January 2026
findings.summary: The OECD's January 2026 Side-by-Side Package maps each jurisdiction's enacted GloBE legislation against OECD model rules, identifying deviations, interpretive choices, and administrative variances across 60+ implementing countries including Luxembourg, Ireland, Switzerland, Singapore, and the UAE.
findings.client_impact: Tax advisers managing MNE holding structures across key IFC jurisdictions (Luxembourg, Switzerland, Singapore, UAE) should use the Side-by-Side Package as a primary reference to identify jurisdiction-specific GloBE deviations that may create unexpected top-up tax liabilities or safe-harbour mismatches.
findings.urgency_reason: Reference tool released; no deadline — recommended immediately for any active Pillar Two structuring or compliance review.
